title: Audit taxonomy: capture policy snapshots, SSO assertions, and actor confidence
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Define an audit event schema and taxonomy that simultaneously captures (1) the exact RBAC policy state at time-of-action (policy snapshot), (2) the SSO/SAML assertion used to authenticate the actor, and (3) a machine-consumable actor confidence score and provenance chain. Motivation: current audit payloads capture actions and target objects but often lack the policy context and identity confidence needed to perform reliable post-hoc authorization reviews or automated policy drift detection. This ticket proposes a compact, signed event envelope that bundles: policy_snapshot (versioned, minimal semantic diff), sso_assertion_snapshot (parsed assertion metadata and thumbprint), actor_provenance (identity_chain, confidence_score, linking hints), and change_scoring (semantic magnitude + safety classification). The envelope must be storage-efficient (compact diffs), privacy-aware (PII redaction policy), and immutable (HMAC or signing reference to canonical store). Deliverables: event schema draft, serialization examples (newline-delimited JSON and compact binary), a prototype serializer in Go and TypeScript, and integration test vectors for common admin flows (grant, revoke, elevate, emergency-access).
acceptance_criteria: Schema document describing the envelope fields and allowed types published to Confluence
Two example serialized payloads: full snapshot and compact diff for a sample role change
Serializer library prototypes (Go + TS) that output NDJSON and compact base64 payloads
End-to-end test demonstrating: user authenticated via SAML -> role grant -> audit event contains policy_snapshot, sso_assertion_snapshot, actor_provenance, and change_scoring
Privacy/redaction rules documented and approved by Privacy/Legal
Security review completed and signing/HMAC approach validated
